nodes.title: Classical-group coordinate comparison
nodes.statement: For V=H^r ⊥ V_an of dimension d over E, identify the paper’s matrix group with SO(V) or U(V) from the shared relevant-pair interface. Here r is the actual Witt index, n=floor(d/2) is only a label, and the standard-dual dimension is N=d−1 for odd SO and N=d otherwise. Transport the flag parabolics and their Levi factors Res_{E/F}GL_j × Isom(V_(j))° with their normalized induction modulus. The quasi-split nonsplit even orthogonal group has r=n−1. All group identifications are over F and commute with localization.
hypotheses: Standing conventions in the reader: characteristic-zero number field F; E=F for orthogonal groups or a quadratic extension for unitary groups; all forms nondegenerate; the input larger dimension d is positive; actual automorphic realizations, rational orbit and measures are specified.
proofSteps: Use the built quadratic Witt decomposition and the requested hermitian analogue, with the specified linear-first/antilinear-first conversion.
Write the block isometry equations in a dual isotropic basis and compare to the determinant-one quadratic group. Compute the modulus using the action on the unipotent Lie algebra.

nodes.title: Bessel stabilizer and Witt index
nodes.statement: For V=H^ell ⊥ V_(ell) and anisotropic w∈V_(ell), the chosen Bessel subgroup is H=Isom(V_(ell)∩w⊥)°, embedded by fixing the flag and w; its defining space has dimension d−2ell−1. If ell<r and w=y_κ in the normal form, the new anisotropic part is the anisotropic part of V_an ⊥ E y_{−κ}. Its Witt index is r−ell when E y_κ is represented in V_an and r−ell−1 otherwise. At ell=r it is the corresponding perpendicular in V_an. For U(V) this H is the subgroup fixing the flag vectors, not the full character stabilizer inside the Levi, which also has a norm-one central torus.

nodes.statement: Given a specified relevant pair W⊂V with V≅H^j ⊥ Ee ⊥ W, choose a>j and set X=H^a ⊥ W and k=a−j−1. Construct a rational Bessel datum of index k in Isom(X)° and an F-isometry of its stabilizer space with V, compatible with the given inclusion W⊂V. Its dimension is 2a+dim W−2k−1=dim V. Export the induced coordinate maps, the rational orbit, localizations and the even-SO normalizer action t=Ad(w_q^k), with w_q²=1. The chosen input on W is σ^t, so that the unfolded inner period has σ.

Record the normalizer element in that coordinate isometry; transport σ only once by t. Proposition 2.6 alone gives occurrence, so the compatibility with a prescribed embedding must be checked as part of this construction.

nodes.title: Bessel–Eisenstein zeta integral
nodes.statement: Let X=H^a⊥W with dim W=m, H_X=Isom(X)°, and P_a its flag parabolic with Levi Res_{E/F}GL_a×H_W. For an irreducible unitary generic isobaric τ on GL_a(A_E) and an irreducible automorphic σ on H_W with a specified realization, use normalized induction I_s=Ind_{P_a(A)}^{H_X(A)}(τ|det|_E^s⊗σ), including δ_{P_a}^{1/2}. Let E(f_s,s) be the meromorphic Eisenstein family, defined from the isobaric inducing data through the imported continuation theory. For a valid rational Bessel datum of index ell on H_X, with stabilizer G and cuspidal realization C_π on G, put Z(s,f_s,v)=P_{ell}(E(f_s,s),v)=∫_[G] B_{ell}(E(f_s,s))(g)v(g)dg. This is the bilinear period. Normalize the compact unipotent quotient to volume 1 and retain a compatible Haar measure on [G].

nodes.statement: In the absolute-convergence chamber, expansion of B_ell(E(f_s,s)) followed by the cuspidal π-period kills every α>0 cell by its nontrivial character, and every remaining nonopen stabilizer cell by a proper constant term of π. nodes.title: Cuspidal module recovery theorem
nodes.statement: Let π be cuspidal of a G-relevant generic discrete global parameter. Assume GenericSummand(π), and assume the exact local GGP distinguished-packet proposition at every localization of its resulting relevant parameter pair (with even-SO outer labels retained). Assume the analytic, convention, classification, spectral and tower inputs specified in TAD.0–5. Then ConcreteModule(π) holds. There is one summand when its allowed outer orbit is a singleton and two distinct summands in the even-SO two-element case. No Whittaker genericity or global cuspidal multiplicity-one hypothesis is imposed.
hypotheses: Standing conventions in the reader: characteristic-zero number field F; E=F for orthogonal groups or a quadratic extension for unitary groups; all forms nondegenerate; the input larger dimension d is positive; actual automorphic realizations, rational orbit and measures are specified.

Convert its Hermitian nonvanishing to the appropriate bilinear dual-and-inverse-character statement. Apply reciprocal nonvanishing with the self-pair numerator to obtain a nonzero critical module; this conversion is essential in the unitary case (G1).
